High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Jabalpur
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
This is first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of the Code of Criminal Procedure for grant of regular bail relating to FIR/Crime No.645/2022 dated 14.10.2022 registered at Police Station Damoh Dehat, district Damoh for the offences punishable under Sections 363, 366,
376(2), 376(D) of IPC and Section 3, 4, 5, & 6/7 of POCSO Act.
Learned counsel for the applicant has submitted that applicant is innocent and has been falsely implicated in the crime in question.
The applicant is in custody since 20.03.2023 and trial will take considerable time to conclude.
He further submits that applicant is permanent resident of district and there is no likelihood of his absconding from the clutches of law or tamper with prosecution evidence.
He also submits that the applicant is ready to furnish adequate surety and shall abide by all the directions and conditions which may be imposed by this Court.

Upon these grounds, the Ramkumar Bansal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196676607/
1 applicant may be released on bail.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the State has opposed the bail application.
Heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the case diary.
According to the prosecution case, the age of prosecutrix at the time of incident was more than 17 months, although the applicant has claimed that she had completed 19 years by that time.

In the statements recorded under Sections 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C. the prosecutrix has stated that she was consensually in love relationship with the applicant and was having physical relationship with him.
Counsel for the objector submits that prosecutrix has no objection, if the applicant is released on bail.

Looking to the facts and circumstances of the case, this Court finds it to be a fit case to release the applicant on bail, therefore, without commenting on the merit of the case, the application is allowed.

It is directed that the applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in a sum of Rs.50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Thousand Only) with one surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the trial Court concerned for his appearance before the said Court on all such dates as may be fixed in this regard during the pendency of trial.

It is further directed that the applicant shall comply with the provisions of Section 437(3) of the Cr.P.C.
Accordingly, this M.Cr.C. stands allowed and disposed of.
(ANURADHA SHUKLA) JUDGE rv Ramkumar Bansal vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 21 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/196676607/
